Build a separate, demo-only Python web app that shows an air quality agent's notifications on a smartwatch face, letterboxed in the browser, with filter chips OUTSIDE the watch frame for switching demo scenarios. Repo: /Users/yashvi/orange_health_assignemnt (you're in an isolated worktree copy). Context: docs/explainer.md (§7.3 restraint, §8 messages, §10 "A night in Delhi") and README.md describe the product. The core Python library in src/aqagent is being built in parallel by others.

Where: only `apps/watch_demo/**`, as its own uv project with its own pyproject.toml, decoupled from the core. Do not edit src/, docs/, the root tests/ or the root pyproject. Add apps/watch_demo/README.md, written for humans.

Stack (the user said Python only): FastAPI + Jinja2 templates, server-rendered, plain CSS. No Node, npm, Next.js or frontend build. Prefer zero JavaScript: chips are links with query params. A few lines of inline JS are fine only if unavoidable.

Look and feel:
- Black letterbox around a centred watch (roughly Apple Watch 45 mm proportions, ~396×484 CSS px, rounded-rectangle bezel). Everything "product" is inside the watch. Everything "demo" sits outside it in the letterbox: the scenario chips, a one-line scenario description, and a small caption "replay of real OpenAQ data".
- Inside the watch: a notification stack, newest first. Each card shows the city, a relative time, the body (≤ 220 chars) and ONE action chip (next_action). Tapping a card opens a "Why?" view inside the watch with 3–4 short plain-English lines built from the explain payload (e.g. "Climbing since 1am", "Well above a normal Delhi morning", "Held overnight (quiet hours), sent at your 06:30 check-in"), plus a back link. The empty state looks like a calm watch face ("All clear in Helsinki"), with an optional "why nothing was sent" line.
- Large type and high contrast. Each card gets a thin accent in its EPA band colour: Good #00e400, Moderate #ffff00, USG #ff7e00, Unhealthy #ff0000, Very Unhealthy #8f3f97, Hazardous #7e0023.

Data contract (the core API will expose exactly this):
- `GET /users` → `[{id, display_name, city, station_id, persona}]`
- `GET /users/{id}/feed?replay_run=<id>&until=<ISO UTC>` → newest-first `[{id, created_at, delivered_at, kind (opened|escalated|cleared|check_in|released), event_kind (spike|climb|elevated|floor|null), band (good|moderate|usg|unhealthy|very_unhealthy|hazardous), body, next_action, decision_id}]`
- `GET /notifications/{id}/explain` → `{decision: {outcome, reason_code, reason, evaluated_at, trigger}, trace: [{layer, passed, reason_code, values}], scores: [...], rules_version}`
- `GET /decisions?user_id&start&end&outcome&replay_run` → rows `{evaluated_at, outcome, reason_code, reason}`

Write a client class that takes its base URL from `AQAGENT_API_URL`. When that's unset, it reads JSON fixtures from apps/watch_demo/fixtures/ that follow the contract exactly. Scenarios go in apps/watch_demo/scenarios.yaml as `{id, label, user_id, replay_run, until, description}`, each one a chip:
1. "Delhi smog night": Arjun (runs 06:30, check-in 06:30, quiet hours 22–07). The night climbs from 1am, the notice is held, then one combined check-in message at 06:30, then "back to normal" at 17:00.
2. "Back to normal": the cleared message on its own.
3. "Helsinki smoke": Aino (asthma, high sensitivity), the smoke episode around 2026-08-24 05:00–09:00 UTC, PM2.5 about 27 vs a usual 4.
4. "Glitch ignored": Mumbai one-hour sensor spikes to ~980 µg/m³. The watch stays calm, with the why line "A 1-hour sensor glitch was ignored".
5. "Quiet night": nothing worth saying (the empty state with a why line).
Messages must read naturally, include past context and exactly one action, and never say "AQI is now 142".

Done looks like:
- `uv run --project apps/watch_demo watch-demo` (a console script) serves on localhost:8100, offline from fixtures.
- pytest tests in apps/watch_demo/tests/ cover: every scenario renders, each card shows exactly one action, the Why view renders from an explain fixture, the empty state, chip links switch scenario, and the client parses contract-shaped JSON (including via httpx MockTransport for the API mode).
- Commit on your worktree branch with messages ending in "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>". Do not push or merge.
- Final report (≤250 words): branch name, commits, how to run it, test result, and any contract fields you needed beyond the list above.

# Air Quality Insight Agent

A service that watches the air in your city so you don't have to, and only speaks up when something is actually worth knowing.

> *"The air's been getting worse since 2am, and it's well above normal for a Delhi morning. Maybe skip the outdoor run today."*
>
> *"Back to normal in Helsinki after a smoky day and a half. Good time to open the windows."*

*(Illustrative examples of the kind of message it sends.)*

---

## The idea

Nobody wants to check an air quality number every hour. People want something that keeps an eye on it for them and taps them on the shoulder when it matters: when the air is turning bad, getting worse, or finally clearing up. They want the reason, and one thing to do about it.

The hard part isn't spotting a high number. The hard part is **restraint**. A useful agent knows what's normal for *your* city, doesn't repeat itself, doesn't wake you up for nothing, and can explain every decision it made, including the times it chose to stay quiet.

This is the first slice of a bigger idea: a proactive personal health agent. Today it watches air quality and sends notifications. The design leaves room for pollen and weather, wearable data like heart rate, other triggers like movement or smart-home sensors, and actions beyond a message.

## How it decides

1. **It learns what's normal for each place.** Every hour it pulls fresh readings from [OpenAQ](https://openaq.org) and learns each station's usual levels for each hour of the day over the last two weeks. A rise from 4 to 15 is a big deal in Helsinki. The same reading is a calm day in Delhi.
2. **It looks for patterns, not thresholds.** It watches for three things: a sudden spike, a sustained climb, and a slow build-up that never looks dramatic in any single hour. It also notices when things return to normal. It ignores sensor glitches.
3. **It checks whether the change matters to your health.** Being statistically unusual isn't enough. The air also has to reach a level that matters on the official air quality scale.
4. **It remembers what it already told you.** Each bad period is one story with a beginning, a middle and an end. You hear about it when it starts, if it gets meaningfully worse, and when it's over. Not every hour in between. It also keeps a daily limit on how much of your attention it uses.
5. **It respects your settings.** You can set quiet hours (only severe air gets through at night), an optional morning check-in, and how sensitive you are. Sensible defaults mean it works without any setup.
6. **It writes everything down.** Every decision is logged with the data and the reasoning behind it, including the decisions to stay quiet. "Why didn't I get warned?" always has an answer.

## Cities

| City | Why it's here |
|---|---|
| Helsinki | Very clean air. Small changes are unusual here. |
| Los Angeles | Clean to moderate, with occasional sharp jumps |
| Bengaluru | Moderate. Home of the team this was built for. |
| Dubai | Naturally dusty from the desert. A high baseline is normal. |
| Delhi | Heavily polluted, and heading into its seasonal smog right now |

## Where things stand

The design is complete and the build is next.

- [x] **How the agent decides**, with diagrams of every layer, at full scope and demo scope: [docs/explainer.md](docs/explainer.md). Start here.
- [x] Requirements, with every point in the original brief traced: [docs/requirements.md](docs/requirements.md)
- [x] Test cases for every requirement: [docs/QA.csv](docs/QA.csv)
- [x] Data source study and storage design: [docs/specs/S-A-openaq-and-schema.md](docs/specs/S-A-openaq-and-schema.md)
- [x] Research into how monitoring tools handle alerts: [docs/specs/S-B-rule-engine-research.md](docs/specs/S-B-rule-engine-research.md)
- [x] The decision rules, calibrated on 90 days of real data: [docs/specs/S-C-rule-engine-spec.md](docs/specs/S-C-rule-engine-spec.md)
- [ ] The service itself (Python)
- [ ] A replay harness that measures what it caught and missed on past data
- [ ] An architecture and decisions note, plus a demo

Setup and run instructions will appear here once the service exists.

## Built with

Python for the service. Possibly a small Next.js page on Vercel for the demo. The design and this repository were developed with Claude Code as a coding partner, and the session transcripts will be included with the submission.

## Data credits

Air quality data comes from [OpenAQ](https://openaq.org) and the original providers listed in [data/samples/stations.json](data/samples/stations.json): AirGradient sensor owners (CC BY 4.0), the US EPA AirNow program (US public domain) and the European Environment Agency (ODC-BY). A 90-day sample is included so the analysis can be reproduced without an API key.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. # CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project status

Greenfield. No code, build tooling, or tests exist yet — only the brief in `docs/` (the PDFs are gitignored and exist only in the local checkout; the summary below is the canonical copy). Once a stack is chosen and scaffolded, add the real build/run/test commands (including how to run a single test) to this file.

- `docs/explainer.md` — **the design source of truth**: the 18-layer model (S1–S3, U1–U3, D1–D8, A1–A2, L1–L2, plus RECORD/REPLAY/GUARD/OPERATE) at full and demo scope, with diagrams and the decision record. Design changes are made here first, closed with the user, then propagated to requirements, specs and QA.csv. Keep audit/review material out of it.
- `docs/requirements.md` — the spec: agreed product vision, v1 scope, decisions log and traceability to every brief requirement. Read it before designing or building; when a decision changes, update its section 8.
- `docs/QA.csv` — test cases, one row each, `requirement_ids` tracing to requirements.md and the brief. Every requirement ID has at least one row. Changing a requirement means updating its rows in the same change; implemented tests should reference their `test_id`.
- `docs/specs/S-A-openaq-and-schema.md` (OpenAQ API facts, chosen stations, storage schema), `S-B-rule-engine-research.md` (sources and rationale), `S-C-rule-engine-spec.md` (the detector, pipeline order, rule format, reason codes and all parameter defaults; the source of truth for decision logic).
- `data/samples/` — 90 days of hourly PM2.5 for the 5 tracked stations plus 2 fixtures (Mumbai glitches, Delhi reference gaps); used for replay and tests without an API key.
- `README.md` is for human readers only: plain prose about what, why and status. Keep agent instructions, internal conventions and spec detail out of it.
- `docs/Assignment_Orange.pdf` — the take-home brief. This is the source of truth for scope.
- `docs/Orange-Invest-JD-Founding-Engineer.pdf` — the role this assignment is for (Orange Invest, Founding Engineer). Useful for judging what the reviewers value: stateful async/event-driven backends, LLM infra (structured outputs, tool calling), queues (Temporal/BullMQ/Kafka/RabbitMQ), Redis, agent-step tracing and token/cost guardrails. Preferred stacks named there are TypeScript/Node.js or Python/FastAPI.

## What we're building: Proactive Air Quality Insight Agent

A backend service that watches air quality continuously and decides on its own when, and what, to proactively tell a user. The product goal is "only speak when something is worth knowing", so restraint (not notifying) is as important as detection.

Data source: OpenAQ (https://openaq.org/), 4–5 cities/stations, polled hourly.

### Core requirements (all mandatory)

1. **Ingestion** — hourly pull of new readings per station, stored with full history (trend detection needs it, not just the latest value).
2. **Insight/trigger logic** — detect patterns, not raw thresholds:
   - sustained trend (climbing for the last N hours)
   - sudden spike (sharp jump vs. recent baseline)
   - return to normal after a bad period
   - explicitly handle false positives and missed triggers
   - **primary detection must be a simple learned anomaly/change-point model on recent history** (e.g. rolling z-score / EWMA residuals, CUSUM, Bayesian online change-point) — fixed thresholds alone don't satisfy this.
3. **Dedup / rate limiting** — persistent per-user state of what has already been said; 6 straight bad hours must not produce 6 identical notifications. Re-notify only on a meaningful change.
4. **Message generation** — short natural-language notification text that references relevant past context and includes exactly one clear next action. Not JSON, not a template like "AQI is now 142", not a pure status update.
5. **Per-city / per-user sensitivity** — baselines differ by location: a user in a clean city gets a lower "unusual" bar than one in a naturally dusty region. Sensitivity should derive from each station's own learned baseline, optionally scaled per user.
6. **Observability** — an internal log/endpoint/dashboard showing what fired, when, why, and the exact data that triggered it, so a bad or missing nudge can be debugged later. Suppressed/deduped decisions should be recorded too, not just sent ones.

Out of scope: polished frontend, auth, multi-tenancy. A few hardcoded users per city is fine.

### Bonus

- Decay/cooldown so the system doesn't nag even after a legitimate re-trigger.
- Evaluation harness that replays historical OpenAQ data and reports interesting moments caught vs. missed. Designing ingestion/detection so it can run against a replayed clock (rather than wall-clock "now") makes this nearly free.

### Submission deliverables

GitHub repo, recorded demo video (e.g. Loom), decision/architecture note, transcript of coding tools/AI used, and conversation/notification history. Keep the architecture note and a notification history export in the repo as the work progresses.

## Domain notes

- OpenAQ reports pollutant concentrations (e.g. PM2.5 in µg/m³), not AQI. AQI must be computed from concentrations (e.g. US EPA breakpoints), and the choice should be documented.
- The current OpenAQ API (v3) requires a free API key sent as an `X-API-Key` header; older v1/v2 endpoints are retired. Keep the key in an env var, never in the repo.
- Station readings can be missing, delayed, or duplicated across polls; ingestion should be idempotent and the detector should tolerate gaps.

242	
243	```
244	  how far above normal (z)
245	   ^
246	   |        SPIKE                 CLIMB                    ELEVATED
247	   |          |                       ___/
248	   |          |\                  ___/                   ______________
249	   |          | \            ____/                  ____/
250	   |   _______|  \______  __/                    __/
251	   |
252	   +-----------------------------------------------------------------------> hours
253	      a sharp jump vs the      rising, hour after        stuck above normal
254	      last few hours           hour                      for many hours, but
255	                                                         not rising
256	      far above normal in      smoothed level above      running total of excess
257	      2 of the last 3 hours    the bar for 3 hours       crosses the bar; resets
258	                               AND the 6h slope is up    once it fires
259	
260	      CLEARING   an open episode has 4 calm hours AND is back to the station's typical band
261	      FLOOR      crossing UP into the person's alert band, whatever is "normal" there
262	```
263	
264	- **One label per event**, by priority: spike, then climb, then elevated. The label drives the wording ("jumped sharply", "getting worse since 2am", "stuck above normal all day").
265	- **Every way of getting worse is covered.** Air goes up fast (spike), keeps rising (climb), or sits high and flat (elevated). Falling-but-still-high isn't a new event. It's the same story continuing.
266	- **Elevated exists to catch what the others miss.** These are slow build-ups that never look dramatic in any single hour.
267	- **The person's sensitivity scales every bar.** Sensitive people get bars 25% lower; people who want fewer messages get bars 25% higher. Station scores are unchanged; only the bar moves.
268

270

272	                 event fires AND the air is at least Moderate

275	       |                                            a calm hour |          | event again, or

279	       |   ^
280	       |   +---- 24h with NO DATA: close quietly, no message (NO_DATA_TIMEOUT)
281	       |
282	       +-- event within 6h of closing --> the SAME episode reopens (no "it's getting bad" again)
283	
284	     NO DATA (under 24h): the episode is frozen. Nothing opens, closes or notifies.
285	                          When data returns, the missing hours are replayed in order.
286	```

292	        |
293	   ---- per STORY -------------------------------------------------------------------

351	**A2 DELIVER.** In the demo, a message is "delivered" when it appears in the person's feed and in the exported history. Real channels come at full scope.

353	---

355	## 9. Learn, and what runs across everything
356	
357	- **L1 FEEDBACK.** A person can mark a message as acted on, dismissed or not useful. In the demo, this is stored and shown next to the decision, and changes nothing.
358	- **L2 ADAPT.** Settings are stored as numbered versions, and every decision records which version it used. A future learning layer will propose a new "learned" version, never edit silently, so every change is visible and reversible.
359	- **RECORD.** Every person gets a decision row for every hour, with an outcome (sent, held, suppressed or no event), a reason code and a stage-by-stage trace of the inputs, values and results. "Why didn't I hear about it at 2am?" always has an answer, as complete as "why did I hear about it?"
360	- **REPLAY.** Nothing in the pipeline reads the real clock, and every hour is recomputed from the readings known at that moment. So replaying the past gives exactly the decisions the live system would have made. Replay is how the rules were tuned, and how caught versus missed moments are measured.
361	- **GUARD.** Not in the demo. At full scope it stands in front of every irreversible action: consent, confirmation and rate limits.
362	- **OPERATE.** Every ingestion run is logged with its freshness, failures and remaining rate limit, so the pipeline's own health is visible.
363

367	
368	The numbers are made up but follow the rules above. Arjun lives in Delhi and runs at 06:30. He has default sensitivity, quiet hours 22:00–07:00, and a check-in at 06:30.

385	           Delhi morning. Maybe skip the outdoor run today and try an indoor workout."
386	 07:00  Unhealthy        -                           quiet hours end; nothing left to release  -
387	 10:00  Unhealthy        -                           same story, same band                     suppressed

402	|---|---|---|---|---|
403	| 1 | One set of layers for both scopes; the demo uses stubs | the demo is the first slice of the product, not a throwaway | a demo-only script | — |
404	| 2 | Station scores are shared and never depend on the person | facts about a place are the same for everyone; personal bars move, scores don't | per-person detection | shared metrics, per-route rules (Prometheus, Alertmanager) |
405	| 3 | DECIDE split into per-story and per-person halves | the split is what prevents fatigue with many signals | one combined restraint step | incident handling (PagerDuty) + notification orchestration (Braze, Airship) |
406	| 4 | "Normal" per station **and** per hour of day, over 14 days | rush hours and nights differ; seasons drift | one average; fixed thresholds | seasonal anomaly baselines (Datadog) |
407	| 5 | Log scale with median and MAD | a doubling means the same everywhere; old spikes don't distort normal | mean and standard deviation | robust statistics |
408	| 6 | "Unusual" and "harmful" are separate scores | a clean city gets a lower bar without harmless alerts | one blended score | anomaly score + a published standard (EPA AQI) |
409	| 7 | EPA bands with NowCast | built for hourly use; one scale for every city | India's 24-hour index (too slow for hourly nudges) | US EPA / AirNow |
410	| 8 | Event shapes: spike, climb, elevated (+ clearing, floor), one label each | matches the brief's trend and spike; elevated catches slow build-ups | thresholds only | control charts: EWMA, CUSUM (NIST) |
411	| 9 | Episodes with hysteresis and a flap guard | one bad period is one story; no on-off-on storms | per-hour alerts with a mute timer | alert states and `for` (Prometheus, Grafana), dedup keys (PagerDuty) |
412	| 10 | Recompute every hour from stored data | replay equals live; late data handled for free | incremental detector state | backtesting |
413	| 11 | Hand-rolled decision pipeline | holding, pacing and episodes aren't covered by any rule library | rule-engine, CEL, ZEN, durable_rules | — |
414	| 12 | Hold overnight and release as one message | a dropped warning is a missed trigger | silences that discard | quiet hours (consumer apps) |

417	| 15 | Messages written by an LLM from verified facts, with a template fallback | natural wording without invented facts; works offline | free-form LLM; templates only | — |
418	| 16 | A 90-day sample ships in the repo | anyone can replay without an API key | live-only | — |
419	| 17 | A sensor silent for 24h closes its episode quietly, with no message | the story can't be finished honestly without data | telling the person the sensor went quiet | — |
